title: Token-provenance validation for FP8/INT8 function-call outputs
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background: During calibration to FP8/INT8 we observe sporadic drift in structured function-call outputs: missing keys, altered enum values, and changes in argument ordering that break downstream callers. Existing schema fuzzing finds many cases but does not capture token-level provenance or the subtle re-serialization differences introduced by mixed-precision kernels.

Goal: Build a targeted validation harness that attaches lightweight token-provenance markers to model outputs, runs calibration profiles (FP8 and INT8), and measures roundtrip fidelity for function-call JSON outputs. The harness will exercise our calibration pipeline, runtime kernel selection, and post-processing (token merging/cleaning) to surface regressions that existing schema checks miss.

Approach:
- Create a small corpus of ~2k prompts covering: nested function-call arguments, optional fields, enum fields, multi-turn function-call sequences, long-argument strings, and edge-case Unicode/escape sequences.
- Instrument model outputs with provenance markers: insert invisible sentinel pairs around argument tokens and function identifiers (non-printing Unicode range reserved for internal testing) so we can track tokenization/merge boundaries across quant modes without changing semantic JSON content.
- Run calibration profiles for baseline (fp32), INT8 calibration, and FP8 calibration using our standard calibration harness and quant profiles.
- Parse outputs with the standard function-calling parser, then perform a roundtrip check: feed parsed output back as prompt (simulating a caller that re-encodes the returned values) and verify identity / minimal edit distance.
- Metrics to collect: schema pass rate (JSON schema validation), function-id stability (same function identifier emitted), argument-set stability (same key set), enum-fidelity (exact matches), token-boundary-shift distribution (measured via provenance markers), and token-level Levenshtein median.
- Thresholds (initial): INT8 schema pass >= 99.0%, FP8 schema pass >= 96.0%; function-id stability INT8 >= 99.5%, FP8 >= 97.0%; median token Levenshtein INT8 <= 3, FP8 <= 6.
- Automated gates: fail CI if INT8 regressions exceed +0.5% compared to baseline or FP8 regressions exceed +1.5% for any high-frequency API pattern.

Deliverables:
- A test harness repo folder (tools/quant-token-provenance-test) with: corpus generator, provenance injector, runner script for calibration profiles, and summary CSV output.
- A Prometheus-compatible exporter that pushes per-profile metrics to the runtime QA dashboard.
- A set of deterministic unit tests and 10 integration scenarios to run in pre-merge CI for runtime-1.25.
- A docs page describing token-provenance markers and how to interpret token-boundary-shift histograms.

Notes / trade-offs: Using non-printing sentinels means the tests rely on tokenization invariants that are not present in customer traffic. That is intentional to amplify boundary issues — we will strip markers from production pipelines. We must also make sure markers do not collide with model tokenization for rare languages; markers chosen are from an unused private unicode range and validated across tokenizers.

Links: Confluence test plan: https://confluence.internal.redwood/quant/provenance-test-plan, GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127, QA dashboard (mock): https://dashboards.redwood/internal/quant-provenance
acceptance_criteria: A harness that runs FP32/INT8/FP8 for the corpus and produces a CSV with the required metrics
INT8 schema pass rate >= 99.0% across the corpus
FP8 schema pass rate >= 96.0% across the corpus
Median token-level Levenshtein within thresholds (INT8 <= 3, FP8 <= 6)
Automated CI gate added to runtime-1.25 that fails on regressions beyond the defined deltas
Documentation and dashboard panels published and linked in the PR
comments: 2026-03-10 Liam Chen: Created ticket to track targeted token-provenance validation. Initial corpus draft attached to GH branch. Assigned to Aisha for implementation.

2026-03-11 Aisha Patel: Prototype provenance injector implemented (uses U+E000..U+E00F range). Ran short smoke tests against the small corpus; observed a cluster of enum-mismatch failures in FP8 for long string args. Filed follow-up ENG-33498 for investigation into tokenizer merging heuristics.

2026-03-12 Marina Kovács (review): Suggest adding roundtrip seeding where parsed JSON is re-serialized by the SDK to catch parser edge cases. Also recommended adding a high-frequency subset (100 prompts) that mimics typical API shapes for gating. Approved approach; please add as tests.
